# Adjudication Task — Chapter 523

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃523화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|스으으으.
  6|
  7|뜨겁다. 단전으로부터 솟구친 열양지기가 사지백해로 뻗어 나가며 혈도를 내달린다. 모든 것이 고요하고 생생하게 느껴진다.
  8|
  9|나는 기경팔맥(奇經八脈)을 따라 공력을 운용했다.
 10|
 11|한 번, 두 번, 세 번…….
 12|
 13|운기조식은 높은 언덕에서 눈덩이를 굴리는 것과 같다. 반복할 때마다 눈덩이는 커진다.
 14|
 15|반면 흙이나 돌, 나뭇가지 등의 이물질이 섞여들 수도 있다.
 16|
 17|이는 곧 공력의 정순함을 흐리는 탁기(濁氣)이며, 운기조식을 반복함으로써 그 탁기를 태우고 정순한 공력이 완성된다.
 18|
 19|‘더, 더, 더.’
 20|
 21|나는 마음속으로 홀린 듯 중얼거리며 운기를 지속해 나갔다.
 22|
 23|자그마치 삼 갑자에 달하는 공력이 화룡의 모습으로 화하여 거침없이 몸 안을 헤엄쳤다.
 24|
 25|내가 그려 낸 심상(心想) 속에서, 화룡의 덩치는 더욱 거대해지고 열기는 뜨겁게 타올랐다.
 26|
 27|그리고 어느 순간 깨달았다.
 28|
 29|‘지금.’
 30|
 31|화륵.
 32|
 33|내 의지에 따라 열양지기가 사방으로 솟구쳤다. 실로 압도적인 열기. 몸 안에서 작은 태양이 터져 나간 것만 같았다.
 34|
 35|감고 있던 눈이 뜨거워지고 코에서는 숨 대신 화염이 흘러나오는 것만 같다.
 36|
 37|아니, 그런 것 같은 것이 아니라 필시 그럴 것이다.
 38|
 39|물이 많으면 넘치는 것처럼, 지금 내 몸 안을 가득 채운 공력은 바깥을 향해 흘러나오고 있었다.
 40|
 41|눈, 코, 입 등. 이른바 칠공(七孔)이라 부르는 일곱 개의 구멍으로부터 흘러나온 열기가 외부를 뜨겁게 달구었다.
 42|
 43|전신 곳곳의 수많은 모공(毛孔)에서도 같은 상황이 벌어지고 있었다.
 44|
 45|스아아아아.
 46|
 47|느껴졌다. 정수리 위로 모여드는 막대한 기의 흐름이. 동시에 나는 머릿속에 펼쳐진 깨끗한 도화지에 그림을 그려나갔다.
 48|
 49|나는 나의 주인이다. 몸 안에 존재하는 혈도 하나, 밖으로 흘러나온 한 올의 기운도 마찬가지다. 전부 내 것이니 주인의 뜻을 거스를 수 없다.
 50|
 51|비록 눈으로 볼 수는 없으나 느낄 수 있었다. 머리 위로 몰려든 열양지기가 주인이 원하는 형태를 취하는 것을.
 52|
 53|하나, 둘, 셋.
 54|
 55|마치 타오르는 것처럼 붉게 물든 세 개의 꽃잎.
 56|
 57|‘삼화취정(三花聚顶).’
 58|
 59|초절정이라는 경지에 깨달음이 더해져 낳은 결과다.
 60|
 61|이것만으로도 천하의 무림인 중 누구나 꿈꾸는 경지지만, 이제 겨우 언덕 하나를 넘은 것에 불과하다.
 62|
 63|후우.
 64|
 65|입술 사이로 짧게 내뱉은 숨결에는 운기조식을 통해 걸러 낸 탁기의 잔재가 스며들어 있다.
 66|
 67|마지막 한 줌의 탁기마저 배출해 냄으로써 공력과 머릿속을 깨끗이 비워 낸 나는, 다음 언덕을 향해 걸음을 내디뎠다.
 68|
 69|‘오기조원(五氣朝元).’
 70|
 71|중단전을 연 후에도 몇 번 시도해 봤지만 끝내 이룰 수 없었던 경지. 내 앞을 가로막은 또 다른 벽.
 72|
 73|‘넘는다. 바로 지금.’
 74|
 75|굳은 결심과 함께 가슴 한구석이 찌르르 울린다.
 76|
 77|지금 잡고 있는 이 긴장의 끈을 놓아서는 안 된다. 괜히 앞뒤 가리지 않고 벽을 맨주먹으로 후려쳐 봤자 주먹만 상하는 법이니까.
 78|
 79|최소한 벽에 실금이라도 가게 하려면 긴장 속에서 정확한 흐름을 읽어야 한다.
 80|
 81|‘조금이라도 방심했다가는 공력이 역류할 가능성이 있어.’
 82|
 83|이미 나 있는 길을 걷는 것은 쉽다.
 84|
 85|그러나 이건 나만의 새로운 길을 개척하는 과정이다. 바위를 치우고, 풀숲을 쳐내야 한다. 절벽을 올라가다가 삐끗하는 경우 역시 있었다.
 86|
 87|공력의 역류는 내상으로 이어지고, 내상을 입은 상태에서 계속 무작정 들이댔다가는 주화입마(走火入魔)에 빠지기 딱 좋았다.
 88|
 89|적천강에게 들은 바에 의하면, 그런 식으로 죽거나 반병신이 된 무림인이 한둘이 아니라고 했다.
 90|
 91|나 역시 암천이 무림에 거대한 똥을 싸대고 있는 지금 휠체어 신세를 질 생각은 없었다.
 92|
 93|‘천천히. 신중하게.’
 94|
 95|다행히 문경과의 수련은 큰 도움이 되었다.
 96|
 97|열화문의 근간이 되는 내공 심법, 열화신공(熱火神功)으로 쌓은 열양지기는 다른 명문 대파의 심법 이상으로 강한 힘과 폭발력을 갖추었지만, 그만큼 움직임이 거친 것이 사실이다.
 98|
 99|그러나 이번 수련을 통해 불완전함을 조금이나마 메울 수 있었다.
100|
101|‘할 수 있다. 정신만 똑바로 차리면 충분히 가능해.’
102|
103|따끈하다. 정수리 위로 삼화취정이 흔들린다. 하지만 걱정하지 마라. 공력은 손보다 빠르니까.
104|
105|‘우선 첫 번째 고리.’
106|
107|내가 신중하게 공력을 움직이기 시작한 바로 그때였다.
108|
109|“공력을 갈무리해라. 어차피 지금 당장은 헛수고다.”
110|
111|“……!”
112|
113|파사삭!
114|
115|갑작스럽게 들려온 누군가의 목소리에 집중력이 깨지자, 오기조원의 형태를 갖춰 가던 공력이 산산이 흩어진다.
116|
117|동시에 찾아온 공력의 역류. 나는 몸속 깊은 곳에서 울컥 솟구치는 위액을 토해 냈다.
118|
119|“오기이이잇!”
120|
121|촤악.
122|
123|소량의 피가 섞인 토사물이 바닥으로 쏟아졌다.
124|
125|시벌, 사진으로 봤던 나이아가라 폭포가 여기 있었네.
126|
127|순간 치밀어 오른 것을 쏟아 내고 숨을 헐떡이는데, 바닥에 오늘 아침에 먹은 반찬들이 나를 향해 손을 흔들고 있다.
128|
129|“우웩, 웨에에엑!”
130|
131|아, 이건 못 참지.
132|
133|몇 번이고 반복해서 한바탕 쏟아낸 후에야 정신이 든 나는, 어느새 멀찌감치 떨어져 있는 가죽신의 주인을 노려보았다.
134|
135|“뭐 하는 겁니까, 지금?”
136|
137|신고 있던 가죽신을 신중히 살핀 문경이 대답했다.
138|
139|“산 지 사흘 밖에 안 된 신발이다. 더러워지면 곤란하지.”
140|
141|“그거 말고요. 왜 운기조식 중에 말 거십니까?”
142|
143|“흔든 것도 아닌데 뭐가 문제냐? 그 정도 경지에 올랐는데도 고작 말 몇 마디로 평정심(平定心)이 깨지는 네놈이 부족한 거다.”
144|
145|“깜짝 놀랐잖습니까!”
146|
147|“나도 깜짝 놀랐다. 도대체 어제 오늘 뭘 처먹었길래 저렇게 많이…….”
148|
149|문경이 눈살을 찌푸리며 바닥에 질펀한 토사물을 바라보았다.
150|
151|“보면 볼수록 더럽군. 모양만 보면 얼추 오기조원의 형상 같긴 해.”
152|
153|“어이, 문 씨!”
154|
155|“뭔 씨?”
156|
157|나는 문경의 서늘한 시선을 피하지 않고 마주 노려보았다.
158|
159|일 초, 이 초, 삼 초.
160|
161|음. 이 정도면 충분한 것 같아.
162|
163|“말이 헛나왔네요. 제가 내상을 크게 입은 모양입니다.”
164|
165|“……네놈을 보고 있자니 기해혈이 다 욱신거린다.”
166|
167|짜게 식은 문경의 눈빛을 피한 나는 황급히 화제를 돌렸다.
168|
169|“그런데 갑자기 무슨 일로, 아니. 그전에 여긴 어떻게 들어오셨습니까?”
170|
171|“문이 왜 있다고 생각하는 거냐?”
172|
173|“하지만 문은 무진이가 지키고 있을…….”
174|
175|말꼬리를 흐린 바로 그 순간.
176|
177|스르륵, 쿵!
178|
179|반쯤 열려 있는 문틈 사이로 한 사람의 신형이 픽 하고 쓰러졌다.
180|
181|못 알아볼 수가 없을 만큼 낯익은 뒤통수에 저절로 눈이 부릅떠졌다.
182|
183|“무진아! 혁무진!”
184|
185|비명을 지르는 내게, 문경이 스산한 목소리로 입을 열었다.
186|
187|“놔두어라. 어차피 흔들어도 일어나지 못할 테니.”
188|
189|흔들어도 일어나지 못한다고?
190|
191|이 피에 미친 살귀가 드디어 일을 냈구나.
192|
193|나는 분노를 담아 버럭 외쳤다.
194|
195|“이 피도 눈물도 없는 살인마! 살성 같은 새끼!”
196|
197|“문을 막고 자고 있길래 깨우려고 했더니 꿈쩍도 안 하던…… 지금 뭐라고 했지?”
198|
199|“예?”
200|
201|“뭐라고 했냐 물었다.”
202|
203|“어?”
204|
205|뭐여, 시벌.
206|
207|때맞춰 혁무진의 시신, 아니 몸이 들썩였다. 힘찬 코골이 소리와 함께.
208|
209|드르렁.
210|
211|“…….”
212|
213|“…….”
214|
215|말없이 허공에서 부딪치는 시선. 나는 매력적인 미소와 함께 입을 열었다.
216|
217|“아주 약간, 사소한 오해가 있었던 것 같습니다.”
218|
219|문경이 메마른 표정으로 대꾸했다.
220|
221|“오해가 아니었던 것 같은데. 사소하지도 않고.”
222|
223|“좋은 게 좋은 거 아니겠습니까.”
224|
225|“죽은 게 죽은 거라고?”
226|
227|“오…… 그게 어떻게 그렇게 되나요?”
228|
229|“안 될 것도 없지. 불만 있느냐?”
230|
231|불만도 있고, 달팽이관에도 큰 문제가 있는 것 같았지만 내겐 그걸 지적할 만한 용기가 없었다.
232|
233|“잘못했습니다.”
234|
235|“사과하면 모두 끝나나?”
236|
237|“진심이 담긴 대화는 모든 응어리를 풀 수 있다고 믿습니다.”
238|
239|“잘됐군. 그럼 암천의 천주에게 가서 대화로 풀어 봐라. 주둥이 찢어 버리기 전에 그 재수 없는 웃음 싹 지우고.”
240|
241|“선조들께서 그러셨지요. 웃는 얼굴에 침 못 뱉는다고.”
242|
243|“퉤.”
244|
245|철퍽.
246|
247|음. 선조들의 말이 틀렸군.
248|
249|하지만 이럴 때일수록 평정심을 되찾아야 한다. 나는 뺨에 묻은 침을 침착하게 닦아 냈다.
250|
251|“발사 속도가 굉장히 빠르시군요. 암기인 줄 알았습니다.”
252|
253|“공력을 실어 뱉으면 사람 눈알 정도는 터트릴 수 있지.”
254|
255|“대단하시네요. 혹시 종족이 저그십니까?”
256|
257|“저승사자다.”
258|
259|“……다시 한번 말씀드리지만, 거듭 죄송합니다.”
260|
261|이 자식을 몇 토막을 내야 잘 죽였다고 소문이 날까, 하는 눈빛으로 나를 바라보던 문경이 작게 혀를 찼다.
262|
263|“됐다. 네놈과 이야기를 나눌 때마다 기가 빨리는군.”
264|
265|“…….”
266|
267|누가 할 말을. 이쪽은 시시각각 생명력이 빨리는 중이다.
268|
269|방금 그 대화로 수명이 사흘 정도는 줄어들었다는 것에 혁무진의 좌심방을 걸겠다.
270|
271|‘혁무진 저 새끼는 호법을 서라니까 그새를 못 참고 또 처자고 있네.’
272|
273|문경도 문경이지만 저놈도 대단한 건 매한가지다.
274|
275|“그런데 여긴 어쩐 일로……?”
276|
277|“또 무슨 개 같은 짓거리를 하려고 찾아왔냐는 뜻으로 들리는군.”
278|
279|“오.”
280|
281|“오?”
282|
283|“오……니요. 그게 오니라 그냥 궁금해서 여쭤본 겁니다.”
284|
285|“못 본 사이 발음이 상당히 이상해졌다고 생각이 드는 건, 기분 탓이겠지.”
286|
287|“그럼요. 기분 탓입니다.”
288|
289|작게 한숨을 내쉰 문경이 손에 든 보퉁이를 던졌다.
290|
291|툭, 반사적으로 받아 낸 내가 눈을 동그랗게 떴다.
292|
293|“이게 뭡니까?”
294|
295|“단환(丹丸)이다.”
296|
297|“단환이요?”
298|
299|봄철 산타클로스인가. 갑자기 웬 선물이래.
300|
301|반신반의하며 보퉁이를 풀어헤치자 작고 단단해 보이는 목갑(木匣)이 하나 나왔다.
302|
303|동시에 콧속 깊숙이 스며드는 기묘한 향기.
304|
305|‘이건…….’
306|
307|단환과 같은 영약은 직접 보기도 전에 그 효과를 안다고 했는데, 지금이 딱 그 경우다.
308|
309|나는 목갑을 열기도 전에 이 안에 든 것이 상당한 효력을 지닌 단환이라는 걸 깨달았다.
310|
311|달칵.
312|

[P118]

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

*Fuck. So this is where the Niagara Falls I saw in pictures were hiding.*

[P57]
I poured out what had come up and stood panting. Then I saw the side dishes I’d eaten that morning waving at me from the floor.

[P58]
“Uweeegh! Bleeegh!”

[P59]
Ah. Couldn’t hold that back.

[P60]
Only after throwing up several more times did I come to my senses. I glared at the owner of a pair of leather shoes, now standing well out of range.

[P61]
“What are you doing?”

[P62]
Mungyeong inspected the shoes on his feet before answering.

[P63]
“I only bought these three days ago. I’d rather they didn’t get dirty.”

[P64]
“Not that. Why did you talk to me while I was circulating my qi?”

[P65]
“I didn’t shake you. What’s the problem? If a few words are enough to break your concentration at your level, you’re the one who’s lacking.”

[P66]
“You startled me!”

[P67]
“You startled me too. What the hell have you been eating yesterday and today to produce so much…?”

[P68]
Mungyeong frowned at the vomit spread across the floor.

[P69]
“The longer I look, the filthier it gets. Though from the shape, it does bear a passing resemblance to Five Qi Returning to Origin.”

[P70]
“Hey, Mr. Mun!”

[P71]
“Mr. *what?*”

[P72]
I held Mungyeong’s cold stare.

[P73]
One second. Two seconds. Three.

[P74]
*Hmm. That should do it.*

[P75]
“Slip of the tongue. I must have suffered a serious Internal Injury.”

[P76]
“Looking at you makes my qi-sea acupoint throb.”

[P77]
I avoided his flat stare and hurriedly changed the subject.

[P78]
“What brings you here all of a sudden? No, wait. How did you get in?”

[P79]
“What do you think the door is for?”

[P80]
“But Mujin’s guarding the door…”

[P81]
My voice trailed off.

[P82]
Slide. Thump!

[P83]
Someone toppled through the half-open doorway. I knew the back of that head anywhere.

[P84]
“Mujin! Hyuk Mujin!”

[P85]
“Leave him,” Mungyeong said in a grim voice. “He won’t wake up even if you shake him.”

[P86]
He wouldn’t wake up even if I shook him?

[P87]
That blood-crazed Killing Ghost had finally done it.

[P88]
“You cold-blooded murderer! You Slaughter Saint bastard!”

[P89]
“He was asleep in front of the door. I tried to wake him, but he wouldn’t budge… What did you just say?”

[P90]
“Huh?”

[P91]
“I asked what you said.”

[P92]
“What?”

[P93]
*What the fuck?*

[P94]
Right on cue, Hyuk Mujin’s corpse—no, his body—stirred. A vigorous snore followed.

[P95]
“Grrrrrr.”

[P96]
“…”

[P97]
“…”

[P98]
Our gazes met in silence. I gave Mungyeong a charming smile.

[P99]
“There seems to have been a very slight, insignificant misunderstanding.”

[P100]
“It didn’t sound like a misunderstanding. Or an insignificant one.”

[P101]
“Can’t we just agree that good is good?”

[P102]
“Dead is dead?”

[P103]
“Oh… How did you get *that* from what I said?”

[P104]
“Why couldn’t I? Do you have a problem with it?”

[P105]
I did. His hearing seemed to have a serious problem too, but I didn’t have the courage to point it out.

[P106]
“I was wrong.”

[P107]
“And an apology settles everything?”

[P108]
“I believe a sincere conversation can untangle any knot.”

[P109]
“Good. Go have one with Dark Heaven’s Lord of Heaven, then. Now wipe that irritating smile off your face before I tear your mouth apart.”

[P110]
“Our ancestors said you can’t spit in a smiling face.”

[P111]
“Ptui.”

[P112]
Splat.

[P113]
*Hmm. Our ancestors were wrong.*

[P114]
At times like this, I had to regain my composure. I calmly wiped the spit from my cheek.

[P115]
“That came out incredibly fast. I thought it was a hidden weapon.”

[P116]
“If I put internal energy behind it, I can burst someone’s eyeballs.”

[P117]
“Impressive. Are you Zerg, by any chance?”

[P118]
“I’m the Grim Reaper.”

[P119]
“…Once again, I’m very sorry.”

[P120]
Mungyeong looked at me as if calculating how many pieces he’d have to cut me into for people to say he’d killed me properly. Then he clicked his tongue.

[P121]
“Enough. Every time I talk to you, it drains me.”

[P122]
*He’s one to talk. I’m losing life force by the second.*

[P123]
I’d bet Hyuk Mujin’s left atrium that conversation had shaved at least three days off my life.

[P124]
*I told that bastard Hyuk Mujin to stand guard. He couldn’t even resist falling asleep again.*

[P125]
Mungyeong was something else, but Mujin was impressive in his own way.

[P126]
“So what brings you here…?”

[P127]
“That sounded like ‘What shitty thing have you come here to do this time?’”

[P128]
“Oh.”

[P129]
“Oh?”

[P130]
“Oh… no. I was just curious.”

[P131]
“Your pronunciation seems to have grown rather strange since I last saw you. Must be my imagination.”

[P132]
“Of course. Just your imagination.”

[P133]
Mungyeong sighed quietly and tossed me the bundle in his hand.

[P134]
Thump.

[P135]
I caught it on reflex and stared.

[P136]
“What’s this?”

[P137]
“A pill.”

[P138]
“A pill?”

[P139]
*Is it Santa Claus in spring? What’s with the sudden present?*

[P140]
I opened the bundle, still unsure what to make of it, and found a small, sturdy-looking wooden case inside. A strange fragrance reached deep into my nose.

[P141]
*This is…*

[P142]
They said you could tell how potent some elixirs were before you even saw them. Now I understood what they meant. I knew the pill inside was powerful before I opened the case.

[P143]
Click.

[P144]
Inside lay a single reddish pill. It looked extraordinary at a glance.

[P145]
I stared at it for a moment, then looked up at Mungyeong.

[P146]
“What are you looking at?”

[P147]
“Why are you giving me something like this all of a sudden?”

[P148]
“It holds a considerable amount of fire qi. It’ll help you.”

[P149]
“What?”

[P150]
“Is there a hidden weapon stuck in your ear? Don’t make me say it twice.”

[P151]
“No, I wasn’t asking what it does…”

[P152]
Mungyeong’s face crumpled. For someone who spent most of his time looking bleak, it was a remarkable display of emotion.

[P153]
“I found it on the way here.”

[P154]
“…?”

[P155]
“Let me correct that. I saw it while passing by and bought it. Satisfied?”

[P156]
*What do you mean, satisfied, old man?*

[P157]
I touched the red pill in its case.

[P158]
*Item check.*

[P159]
Ding.

[P160]
> **System**
>
> Mungyeong’s Specially Crafted Pill for Jin Taekyung
>
> Would you like to view more detailed information?
>
> **Y / N**

[P161]
*Yeah. No. That’s enough.*

[P162]
I closed the small System window and gave Mungyeong a lukewarm look.

[P163]
“‘Saw it while passing by and bought it.’ Right.”

[P164]
“…What’s that look for?”

[P165]
“Nothing. Thank you. I’ll take it.”

[P166]
What I felt toward Mungyeong was half gratitude, half fear.

[P167]
*I appreciate the good pill, but what the hell is the next training session going to be…?*

[P168]
Being treated this well all of a sudden felt like being fed a good meal before an execution.

[P169]
As if he understood what my trembling gaze meant, Mungyeong opened his mouth.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
